task: METRIC-MECHANISM THINKER (ideas_29sep): <= 5 changes whose expected sign is positive on ANY embryo by construction, from the official metric code + exp85a pipeline; no public fitting; local files only
summary: Verdict: no new change is positive on any embryo by construction AND can be built and dummied by morning. The night plan (risk stack K + SEC n2a + DIS 2.25 [+CI], exp75, exp89p) should stay as it is. How this was checked: I re-read the official scorer (tools/official metrics.py, division_metrics.py, io.py, and tracksdata DistanceMatching, which does optimal one-to-one matching with weights 1/(1+d)). I then ran a structural audit of the exp85a dummy CSV: 0 merge nodes, 0 nodes with out-degree >= 3, 0 edges with dt != 1, 0 duplicate edges, 1 isolated node and 1 same-frame exact-duplicate coordinate pair. So the provably-useless-node or edge class holds about 2 items (EV ~1e-6), which matches the I-221 closure. Every other node-drop group (border, z-edge slices, synthetic, readmitted, short components) is already measured as too heavily annotated to pay (I-147/I-148/I-312/I-331). Annotated test tracks are chosen independently of our detections, so no node class is provably unannotated. Chained forks, where one fork can only be a redundant duplicate of another under the +-1-frame rule, number 0-2 on 4 clips, so that EV is ~0. The code shows two asymmetries that no earlier record lists. (A) Edges with dt != 1 are dropped before edge scoring, but the division scorer uses the raw out-degree and successors. A skip-frame daughter edge therefore costs 0 on the edge term and 0 nodes but still counts as a fork (MM-1). (B) The edge scorer keeps only the 2 lowest edge ids per source, while the division scorer sees every child. A third hedge child is invisible to edges (MM-2). Neither is construction-positive on the division term. MM-1 still pays the usual fork break-even, precision J/(1+J) ~0.16-0.27, and its candidate pool is mostly fragment restarts. MM-2 carries cross-component, edge-order and validator risks and is a metric-artefact exploit. Both need new code with no lab test, so neither is feasible or advisable for 29 Sep; MM-1 is the one worth a post-deadline lab test. Of the current knobs, only DIS 2.25 has a construction-positive part: its node term, about -0.7% nodes, which is ~+0.0006-0.0007 on any embryo. Its edge term is unknown, and it is already in the night stack (MM-3). Notes: research/wf_ideas_v4/ideas_29sep/mine_mechanism.notes.md; scripts in the session scratchpad (audit_graph.py, dt2_supply.py, fork_chain.py).

candidates.idea: Skip-frame (dt=2) daughter fork: for a parent P at t (out-degree 1) and an orphan track start C at t+2 with no t+1 candidate, add edge P->C instead of a synthetic t+1 daughter node. The edge term and node count are unchanged by construction; the edge counts only for the division term.
candidates.source: Mechanism reasoning from tools/official/src/tracking_cellmot/metrics.py l.71-87: _evaluate_matched_graph keeps only edges with t_target - t_source == 1, before the 2-child cap and before FP/TP counting. division_metrics.py l.354-357, l.264 and l.465-468: pred forks = out_degree >= 2 on the raw graph, and lineages = {child, successors(child)}, with no dt filter. A child at t+2 can match the GT grandchild at t+2 (daughter lineage = GT child + grandchildren, l.219). Supply on the exp85a dummy: 3,074 orphan starts; 2,306 have an out-degree-1 node <= 9 um at t-2; 197 have one only at t-2.
candidates.how: New builder patch, e.g. --patch dt2fork, after the DaughterNet insertion. For each orphan start C (in-degree 0, t >= 2) with no admissible t-1 parent, pick P at t-2 with out-degree 1, |P-C| <= SAFE_DIV_MAX_UM, a sister (P's t-1 child) within SAFE_DIV_SISTER_MAX_UM of C, and a per-clip cap (e.g. 3). Write P->C as the last edge row. It also needs the x138 OUTPUT_ENFORCE_NEXT_FRAME / cell-12 next-frame asserts relaxed for these edges only. No env knob exists for this.
candidates.why_not_public_fit: No value is read from the board. The only free parameters are geometric gates copied from the existing safe-division knobs and a cap. The mechanism comes from the scorer code.
candidates.expected_effect: Edge term: exactly 0 (dropped before scoring). Node term: 0 (no node added). Division term: each added fork is TP, FP or free, like any insertion, so the sign needs precision above J/(1+J) ~0.16 (lab) to ~0.27 (public). The t+2 pool is mostly tracking-fragment restarts (B20 anatomy: only ~3/30 GT daughters are undetected at t+1), so without a ranker precision is likely below break-even. Size at a cap of 3 per clip is at most about +-0.001. NOT construction-positive.
candidates.status_in_our_records: Untried. Not in ideas.json (checked for skip-frame, dt, out-degree and midpoint). Related but different: I-172 gap closing uses midpoint nodes (dt=1), and I-276 notes that the metric absorbs +-1 frame. Risks: the Kaggle CSV validator may reject dt != 1 edges (unverified, so an ERROR could cost a slot); new code with no lab after the R8 cut; the DaughterNet score is trained on t+1 daughters, so it cannot rank these candidates. Post-deadline lab item only.

candidates.idea: Third-child hedge fork: on an existing insertion or safe-division fork P->{A, B}, add a third edge P->B2 to the next-best orphan daughter candidate, written as P's highest edge id. The edge scorer drops out-edges beyond the 2 lowest ids, but the division scorer's lineage bipartite matching sees all 3 children, so a wrong B can be rescued by B2.
candidates.source: Mechanism reasoning from metrics.py l.137-153: the out-degree cap keeps the two lowest EDGE_IDs per source, applied only in edge scoring. division_metrics.py l.264-271: pred_lineages covers all successors, with max bipartite matching of >= 2 GT lineages. l.477-490: the cross-component rule scans all children.
candidates.how: New patch in the DaughterNet insertion (tools/div_insert.py, builder --patch divinsert): keep the top-2 daughter candidates per inserted fork. Emit the continuation edge, then B, then B2 last in the CSV edge rows. B2 must be an orphan start (in-degree 0), otherwise the fork becomes malformed. Cap it at the existing DIVINS_CAP 6. No env knob exists.
candidates.why_not_public_fit: No value is read from the board. It uses the existing insertion's second candidate.
candidates.expected_effect: Division: a gain when B is wrong and B2 is right (an FP 'considered' fork becomes TP, ~+0.002 per public TP). A loss when B2's direct-child evidence falls in another annotated GT component, which makes the whole fork an invalid FP and can kill a would-be TP. Edges: 0 only if the Kaggle loader assigns edge ids in CSV row order. Otherwise a continuation TP edge on an annotated track may be the one dropped, costing roughly -0.0001 per case with a large tail. Node term 0. Not construction-positive.
candidates.status_in_our_records: Untried; not in ideas.json. NOT RECOMMENDED. (1) The edge-id order in the hidden scorer is unverified. (2) The scorer may reject out-degree > 2, since the metric code only warns, and the host wrapper is unknown. (3) The metric code calls out-degree > 2 'biologically invalid'; exploiting the edge-versus-division cap asymmetry is the same kind of thing as the July WCC 'metric hack' that the hosts patched, and it carries reputational and eligibility risk. (4) It is new code with no lab. At most a post-deadline note.
